name: Nora Alvarez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43, a senior developer leading school-meals software at a tech company, with a master’s degree. I know the code and the kitchen handoffs well, and I review every allergy change before release. Salma works as a school caretaker; we have a mortgage and two school-age children, but a flood repair left less than one month of bills saved despite my lead job’s lower-than-usual pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the school-meals team a small AI helper can tidy repeated checks, but a child with an allergy needs the right lunch, not a plausible answer. I try AI sometimes on fake orders, and I still sign the release myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead developers and have a master’s degree, but this company pays below the usual lead rate. My wife Salma is a school caretaker; we have two children, a mortgage and less than one month saved after a flood repair, so ordinary bills already worry me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep reviewing allergy-order code and ask the meal staff for the three most common corrections. We would stop paying for the extra sports channel and put 24 monthly into the food account while both wages continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about the mortgage even in this quiet AI world. A small software gain cannot rebuild the cash the flood took.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What mistake scares you most?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A kitchen once saw a dairy-free mark vanish after a menu change. A worker caught it at the tray, and I traced the fault before lunch the next day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why stay with lower pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The few similar jobs nearby do not all pay better, and the school schedule fits our family. I have asked for a raise, but I will not count one until it is approved.

I use **AI occasionally** on fake orders, then sign the result myself.
think: I have **under one month saved** after a flood repair.
I know my **low lead pay** and mortgage make ordinary bills tense.
do: **Keep reviewing** allergy-order code and collect meal-staff corrections.
**Cancel the sports channel** and redirect 24 monthly to food while wages continue.
feel: **Anxious already** about mortgage costs and thin savings.
S0.quote: A small software gain cannot rebuild the cash the flood took.
fieldNote: Her strong **lead skill** does not erase the household’s flood-related cash gap or the monthly pressure of a mortgage.
The **allergy release** matters because a child could receive the wrong meal.

steps.text: Keep reviewing school meal allergy code and staff corrections
Cancel the extra sports channel and reserve 24 monthly for food

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI taking code, buying and answering parents will reach our meal platform early. I would bring the staffing question to our workers’ council and demand a clear human check for allergies.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can lead the hard incidents, but management may use faster code to leave vacant developer seats empty. I think my own hours or pay could shrink when they ask one lead to cover more schools, and Salma’s caretaker wage will not carry our mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d learn a new AI method for checking menu changes against allergy rules using fake school orders, after another engineer shows me how it works. In the first year I’d take the staffing and release-signoff numbers to the workers’ council; I’d seek paid lead roles in other towns only if interviews are arranged before travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious and angry about a smaller team carrying the same blame. I can learn a tool, but I cannot make our mortgage smaller by typing faster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which number would you take to the council?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How many schools each engineer checks before and after the change, and who answers for an allergy error. I want those numbers on paper before we call the new rota efficient.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can you afford travel for interviews?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only one trip at a time after an employer confirms an interview. I would apply from home first, because we do not have spare money for speculative journeys.

I would bring these questions to our **workers’ council**.
think: I expect **empty developer seats** and more schools per lead.
I fear my **own pay or hours** could shrink while Salma’s wage cannot cover the mortgage.
do: **Learn AI allergy checks** on fake orders after an engineer demonstrates the method.
**Bring staffing figures** to the workers’ council in the first year.
**Apply for lead roles** from home; travel only after an interview is confirmed.
feel: **Anxious and angry** about my own hours and team accountability.
S1.quote: I cannot make our mortgage smaller by typing faster.
fieldNote: She links **headcount** to the number of schools each remaining engineer must check.
Her external search limits **travel costs** until a paid-role interview is confirmed.

steps.text: Learn AI allergy checks on fake orders after a colleague demonstrates them
Bring school-to-engineer figures to workers council talks
Apply for paid lead roles remotely and travel only for confirmed interviews

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could do the code, planning and checking I lead, and our company owes workers a written plan. Robots for hands-on school kitchens and caretaker work may arrive around 2031, so my desk role faces the earlier date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my lead wage could end before we rebuild even a month of bills. Salma’s caretaker work might last a few more years, but one wage cannot cover our mortgage and two children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the workers’ council now to seek written notice and paid retraining terms, and Salma and I would list which bills leave the account first. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my role ends, I’d apply for paid food-safety software support only where vacancies exist and wages cover our bills; I’d call the lender before arrears if the search ran long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed and short of sleep. A senior title does not fill the fridge after a pay cheque stops.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say the company may not need my coding role, but that does not mean the house disappears tomorrow. I would cancel the family weekend trip and keep the food and mortgage paid first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take an unpaid course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No; the household cannot spare wages. I would take training only if it is paid time and linked to a real opening, not just a certificate.

say: I want a **written worker plan** for full AGI by 2028.
I know **kitchen and caretaker robots** follow the earlier screen-work change around 2031.
think: I expect my **lead wage** could end before savings recover.
I know Salma’s **caretaker wage** alone cannot pay the mortgage and children’s bills.
do: **Seek written notice** and paid retraining terms through the workers’ council now.
**List upcoming bills** with Salma and cancel the trip if my wage stops.
**Apply** for bill-covering food-safety vacancies after 2028 displacement; call lender before arrears if search runs long.
feel: **Alarmed and sleepless** about losing the household’s main wage.
S2.quote: A senior title does not fill the fridge after a pay cheque stops.
fieldNote: Her **2028 desk-work risk** arrives before robots reach school kitchens and caretaking.
The **lender call** is conditional if a long search risks arrears, and provides no assumed income.

steps.text: Ask workers council for written notice and paid retraining terms
Cancel the family weekend trip if developer wages stop
Apply for paid food-safety support vacancies if displaced after 2028 and pay covers bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years before full AGI in 2031 gives us time to teach someone how an allergy exception actually reaches a kitchen. Robots for hands-on meal work may follow around 2034, but my code changes first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn more about food-safety disputes while I still earn, though full thinking AI may handle those too. Salma and I might rebuild an emergency account if both wages hold and no new house repair arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the school meal service for two anonymized allergy incidents each month to study with a kitchen supervisor, only if both employers approve paid time. We would save 90 monthly while both wages continue; if my developer role ends after 2031, I’d seek paid food-safety support only where vacancies remain and wages cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious but able to prepare. A written lesson from a kitchen incident is worth more to me than a promise of a safe job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you study in an incident?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The menu change, the allergy mark and the moment the tray was stopped. I would ask the supervisor which check a tired worker could still do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the school says no?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my lead job and ask for past incident reports with names removed during paid work time if my own manager agrees. I would not call a visit completed when it never happened.

say: I want **kitchen incidents** taught before AGI reaches the code in 2031.
I know **meal-work robots around 2034** follow the screen-work shift.
think: I might learn **food-safety disputes**, though AGI could take the reasoning.
I could rebuild **emergency savings** if both wages continue.
do: **Study** two incidents monthly with both employers’ paid approval; otherwise review anonymized reports if my manager grants paid time.
**Seek paid food-safety support** only if displaced after 2031 and vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Anxious but prepared** if approved real cases are available.
S3.quote: A written lesson from a kitchen incident is worth more to me than a promise of a safe job.
fieldNote: Her practice needs **two employers’ approval** and paid time with real anonymized incidents.
The **90 saving** is independent of training and depends on both wages.

steps.text: Study monthly incidents with both employers’ paid approval; otherwise review old reports with manager-approved paid time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 is time to repair the household buffer and make allergy rules understandable to every kitchen. Robots for hands-on meal work may follow around 2039, after code and planning change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children would be older, but I will not rely on their wages to pay the mortgage. I could build six months of bills if both incomes continue, even though my developer job might change by 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep leading the meal platform and write a plain checklist for every allergy bug my team fixes, using no child names. Salma and I would save 130 monthly when both wages allow; if my role ends after 2036, I’d seek paid school-food support only where vacancies remain and pay covers the mortgage and basic bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about this year’s thin savings even with a longer warning. Ten years helps me make a plan. The flood bill is still in the account today.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would use the checklist?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The developer who changes the menu code and the kitchen worker who sees the tray. I would ask each to mark which step was unclear before we call it finished.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for a new lead role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a written offer that covers the new housing payment and both children’s school travel. Few similar jobs are nearby, but we would not move on a rumour.

I know **kitchen robots around 2039** follow the thinking-work change.
think: I will not count on **children’s future wages** for the mortgage.
I might build **six months saved** if both household incomes hold.
do: **Keep leading meal software** and write checklists without child names.
**Seek** bill-covering food support after 2036 displacement; move only for written pay covering new housing and children’s school travel.

S4.quote: The flood bill is still in the account today.
fieldNote: Her **current flood cost** keeps the longest scenario anxious, even while the 2036 date gives her more time to plan.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my lead wage could disappear before we rebuild a month of savings. Written notice, paid retraining and a real food-safety support vacancy that pays our bills would help; I would speak to the lender before arrears if needed.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who would check the child’s tray after software has made a decision. I want the kitchen worker to have a clear stop rule and a named developer to answer for the code. An allergy alert needs a kitchen worker with a stop rule and a developer who answers for the code.

headlineQuote: An allergy alert needs a kitchen worker with a stop rule and a developer who answers for the code.
portrait: Nora is a **43-year-old senior developer** with a master’s degree, below-usual lead pay and less than one month saved.
She and Salma cover **two children** and a mortgage, after a flood repair emptied their buffer.
She uses AI **occasionally after proof**, while reviewing allergy releases herself.
She asks a **workers’ council** for staffing facts, written notice and paid learning.
The **2028 scenario** most threatens her wage before later robots reach kitchen and caretaker work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her lead wage before the family rebuilds savings.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, paid retraining, a bill-covering food-safety opening and early lender contact would help.
